title: Best Flooring for Garage Conversions, ADUs and DADUs in Snohomish
meta: For Snohomish garage conversions and ADUs, rigid core vinyl plank over a tested, sealed slab wins on moisture, cold and renters. Prep steps and prices from Wills Flooring.
keywords: best flooring for garage conversion, ADU flooring ideas, DADU flooring over concrete slab, flooring for converted garage cold floor, vinyl plank installation Snohomish WA

blocks.lead: For almost every Snohomish garage conversion, ADU or DADU, the best floor is rigid core vinyl plank installed over a moisture-tested and sealed slab. It handles the cold concrete, the damp, the renters and the dog, and it costs $2.50 per sq ft in labor to install.
blocks.detail: The floor is the easy part. What decides whether it lasts is what happens to the slab first: a garage slab was poured to hold a truck, not a bedroom, and a new DADU slab is still drying for months after the framers leave.

blocks.html: Snohomish County has made it much easier to add an ADU or a detached DADU, and around Clearview, Fobes Hill and the acreage east of town we see a steady stream of two-car garages becoming rentals, in-law suites and studios. The flooring question comes late and is usually asked as: can I just put something over the concrete? You can, but the concrete is the whole problem.

blocks.text: Why a garage slab is different from a house floor

items.title: No vapor barrier, or a torn one
items.text: Older Snohomish garage slabs were often poured straight on gravel, and ground moisture wicks up through them all winter. The plank does not care, but the adhesive, the underlayment and any framing on the slab do. We test every slab before quoting.

items.title: It slopes toward the door
items.text: Code requires a garage slab to drain outward, typically an inch or two over the bay. A floating floor follows that slope and every piece of furniture leans. Self-leveler or a framed subfloor fixes it, and it is the biggest prep cost on most conversions.

items.title: It is cold and uninsulated
items.text: Concrete on grade sits near ground temperature, about 45°F in a Snohomish February. Plank directly on it feels cold through socks. An insulated sleeper subfloor or a plank with a thick attached pad makes the room livable.

items.title: Oil, salt and old paint
items.text: Decades of drips and de-icer soak into concrete. Sealers and adhesives will not bond to a contaminated slab. Degreasing or grinding and a bond test come before any product decision.

blocks.text: Slab prep, in the order it has to happen

items.text: A relative humidity probe or calcium chloride test over 72 hours. New DADU slabs often read high for six months after the pour; old garage slabs read high all winter. The number decides whether a roll-on sealer comes first.
Degrease oil spots, remove paint and old sealer, grind high spots at cracks and cold joints. Skip this and the leveler will not bond.

Self-leveler brings a sloped bay flat within 3/16 inch over 10 feet, which floating plank needs. On a deep slope, a framed sleeper subfloor with rigid foam between the sleepers is often cheaper and adds insulation.

Rigid core plank with an attached pad, floated with expansion gaps at every wall and around the plumbing for the kitchenette. A 900 sq ft two-car garage unit is 900 × $2.50 = $2,250 in labor, plus prep and material.

blocks.text: Room by room inside a Snohomish ADU

items.html: Entry and mudroom corner. On acreage, tenants track in mud and dog hair. Run the same rigid plank to the door and add a recessed or heavy mat. No transitions to catch grit.
Kitchenette and bath. The same plank, with silicone at the tub, toilet flange and under-sink cabinet. One continuous floor is easier to clean between tenants and has no seams to fail.
Bedroom. Plank plus a large rug is our usual recommendation. Carpet is warmer but on a slab it needs a framed subfloor to stay dry, and it rarely survives two tenant turnovers.
Attached ADU sharing a wall or ceiling. A plank with a thicker acoustic pad keeps footfall down for the main house. Above a garage, this matters more than anything else here.
Wood stove or pellet stove. Common in Snohomish outbuildings. Keep the plank outside the hearth clearance in the manufacturer's manual and use tile or a hearth pad there.

blocks.text: When vinyl plank is the wrong call, and what we will not do

a.title: Plank is right when
items: The slab tests dry or has been sealed
The floor has been leveled or framed flat
The unit will be rented or used hard
You want one floor through wet and dry rooms
Budget needs to cover the whole unit at once

b.title: We hold off when
items: The slab reads wet and the owner wants to skip the sealer
Water enters at the old garage door threshold in heavy rain
The conversion has no permit and the slab was never inspected for the new use
The room is a true workshop where a floating floor will be gouged
Radiant heat is planned but not yet installed

blocks.title: The DADU trap:
blocks.text: A brand-new slab is not a dry slab. Concrete keeps releasing water for months, and a floor installed the week after drywall often traps that moisture. If your Snohomish DADU is on a fresh pour, either wait for a passing test or budget for a moisture sealer. We covered the test itself in does vinyl plank need a moisture test over concrete.
Checklist before you order flooring for the conversion

items: Get the slab moisture reading in writing, with the date and method.
Ask how the slope will be handled: leveler, sleepers or both, and what each costs.
Decide on insulation now; it is nearly impossible to add under a finished floor.
Choose a rigid core plank with at least a 20 mil wear layer if the unit will be rented.
Plan expansion gaps around the kitchenette plumbing and at the old garage door opening.
Confirm where the wood stove hearth ends and the plank begins.
Get the 1-year workmanship warranty and the plank's waterproof warranty on the same written quote.

faq.q: Can I put vinyl plank directly on a garage floor?
faq.a: Only if the slab is flat, clean and tested dry. Most garage slabs slope toward the door and were poured without a vapor barrier, so they need leveling and often a moisture sealer first. The plank itself is fine on concrete; the prep is what makes it last.

faq.q: How do I make a converted garage floor warmer?
faq.a: The best fix is a framed sleeper subfloor with rigid foam between the sleepers, then plank on top. It raises the floor a few inches but transforms comfort. The lighter option is a rigid core plank with a thick attached pad, which takes the edge off but does not insulate the slab.

faq.q: What does it cost to floor a two-car garage conversion in Snohomish?
faq.a: Installation labor for vinyl plank is $2.50 per sq ft, so a 900 sq ft unit is 900 × $2.50 = $2,250 in labor. Slab leveling, sealer or a sleeper subfloor, plus the plank itself, are quoted at the free estimate after we test the slab. Prep is usually the larger number on a conversion.

faq.q: Is laminate okay in an ADU?
faq.a: It can be, on a dry slab and away from the kitchenette and bath. Laminate has a fiberboard core that swells if slab moisture or a dishwasher leak reaches it and never recovers. For a rental with a wet room, rigid core vinyl plank at the same $2.50 labor rate is the safer floor.

faq.q: Do I need radiant heat under an ADU floor?
faq.a: No, but if you want it, install it before the floor. Electric mats or hydronic tubing in a topping slab both work under rigid core vinyl plank, as long as the plank is rated for it and the surface stays under about 85°F. Adding radiant later means pulling the floor up.

faq.q: Will the county inspect the flooring in my ADU?
faq.a: The floor covering itself is not usually inspected, but the slab and any framed subfloor can be part of the permit, and an unpermitted conversion is a problem at resale. We are happy to install on a permitted project and will tell you if the slab looks like it was never meant for living space.
